title: Optimize: Quality-gate spec for eval-driven rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a minimal, production-ready quality gate for Redwood Optimize that controls model rollouts and automated promotions using eval signal. This ticket is the product spec and acceptance criteria for v1 of the Optimize Eval/Quality subsystem.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic pass/fail rules for automated model promotion (canary -> gradual -> global).
- Standardize prompt set composition and metric definitions to ensure reproducible regressions.
- Define A/B criteria and sample size requirements to avoid noisy promotions.
- Define automatic rollback triggers and human-in-the-loop escalation paths.

What this PRD covers (v1 scope):
- Prompt sets: canonicalization, labeling, and storage schema for scoring. Each model variant will be evaluated on the same curated prompt sets before rollout.
- Metrics: primary success metric (Task Success Rate - TSR), secondary metrics (latency median, hallucination rate, toxicity flag rate).
- Thresholds: numeric regression thresholds and statistical significance rules that determine pass/fail.
- A/B test rules: minimum sample size, confidence criteria, minimum exposure window.
- Rollback rules: automatic revert and alerting conditions for severe regressions or safety hits.

Out of scope for v1 (deferred):
- Automated prompt set generation and dynamic weighting by customer.
- Full ML fairness analyses and adversarial attack detection.
- Auto-tuning of thresholds via meta-learning.

Rationale: Teams running Dedicated and Private deployments have asked for clear, auditable criteria so that rollouts are repeatable across customers and environments. A deterministic quality gate reduces manual review load while enabling fast safe rollouts for high-confidence changes.
scope: In scope: prompt set curation pipeline (static sets), scoring functions, baseline generation for each model family, threshold config UI, automated rollback action in rollout infra. Out of scope: on-device evals, customer-provided prompt training or personalization in v1.
changes: Since initial brainstorm (2026-02), we narrowed metric set to a single primary metric (TSR) plus 3 safety/perf secondaries to simplify decision logic and speed implementation. Removed continuous learning autopromote feature from v1 due to infra constraints.
acceptance_criteria:
1) There exists a canonical prompt set format (JSONL) and at least three curated prompt sets (chat, instruction-following, retrieval-augmented) stored in Optimize artifacts.
2) Eval job runs produce a results blob with primary and secondary metrics for any candidate model; results schema documented.
3) Quality gate config supports: primary metric threshold, delta threshold vs baseline, p-value cutoff, and minimum sample size.
4) Default v1 thresholds: primary metric delta <= -1.5% triggers fail; absolute primary metric drop >= 2.5% triggers automatic rollback during canary. Secondary metric increase (latency median +20ms or hallucination rate +1.0 percentage point) flags human review.
5) A/B experiments require >= 5,000 aggregated requests or 24 hours of exposure (whichever is larger) before promotion; observed uplift must be >=1.5% and p<0.05.
6) When rollback triggers, rollout infra must revert traffic to previous stable model within 5 minutes and create an incident ticket linking the eval output.
7) UI surfaces pass/fail status, metric diffs, and raw eval artifacts for audits.
8) Documentation and runbook exist for SRE/PM/Support describing investigator steps and appeal process for blocked rollouts.
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Opted to use Task Success Rate (TSR) as primary metric to unify across generation and classification flows.
2026-03-04: Chose conservative default thresholds to minimize customer-facing regressions (see acceptance_criteria).
2026-03-08: Deferred auto-prompt generation to v2 after eng capacity review.

notes:
Implementation risks: small customers may never hit sample-size thresholds — fallback is to require manual review instead of auto-promote. Need explicit audit trail to satisfy enterprise customers.
Operational cost: running full prompt set evals for every candidate increases infra costs; explore selective short-circuiting for obviously smaller changes (diff-based heuristics) in v2.
